chapter: Touring, recording and Fletcher's band in the 1940s
title: Singer Viola Jefferson, who outsang Ella with 'A-Tisket A-Tasket'
summary: Fletcher conducted one Horace Henderson date; singer Viola Jefferson brought the house down at the Chicago Savoy with 'A-Tisket A-Tasket' by selling it with motions.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: I notice that some of these arrangements -- most of them indicated in here are by you, although one or two, like you did I Got Rhythm in February of 1940, and that was Fletcher's arrangement.
Let's see now. This is interesting. Yeah. And there's another one in here where it says Fletcher Henderson conducts Horace Henderson and his orchestra. That
was "Oh Boy, I'm in the Groove."
Oh yes. I had a little singer with me named Viola Jefferson, a girl. Does it state that on there?
Yes. She went to Europe, and was quite successful there. She was the girl that outsang Ella Fitzgerald on "Tisket-a-Tasket" with that 5,000 people in the Savoy Ballroom in Chicago.
What do you mean she outsang her? She --

She took her own number that she made famous and brought the house down. Not because of the fact that she was a local girl, but she really did a job. But she sold, you know, Ella just stood up and sang at that time. This little girl -- "Tisket-a-Tasket" -- did (unintelligible) motions with it. It was a funny thing, you know. We knew that she didn't have the voice or the potential that Ella, but this little girl had drive. She was a saleslady, we'll call her. She knew how to put a tune over. She stayed with me quite a while. She was quite a vocalist.
